standard: GDD rework v2 · 80+ researched scenarios · scorecard-passed
note: Anyone can do anything, whatever their gender (UNESCO 3.2). Retrofit of the v1 library (was 71% single-mechanic) to v2. Builds on g04.

categories.anyone-be: Anyone can be it (try on any job)
categories.dream: Dream big; ability grows with practice
categories.no-limit: No one decides your dream by gender

evidenceBase: Children draw scientists gender-equally at 5-6 but skew male by 7-8: occupational stereotypes set early, so 3-6 is the window
Counter-stereotype role models (women in STEM, men in care) raise children's interest and ability beliefs
India's leaky pipeline: women are ~43% of STEM grads but ~27% of the STEM workforce; care work is heavily feminised, so boys-in-care matters too

scenarios.hook: Lensy opens the dress-up box. Be a doctor!
scenarios.relearn: Anyone can be a doctor, girl or boy.

scenarios.hook: Try on the pilot's cap!
scenarios.relearn: Anyone can fly a plane; women are pilots too.

scenarios.hook: Match each kid to the job they dream of.
scenarios.relearn: Any kid can dream of any job.

scenarios.hook: Pop on the chef's hat!
scenarios.relearn: Anyone can be a chef and cook delicious food.

scenarios.hook: "Doctors are men and nurses are women."

myth.un: Doctors are men; nurses are women.
myth.re: Anyone can be a doctor or a nurse.
myth.why: The job needs skill and care, not a gender.

scenarios.relearn: Doctors and nurses can be any gender.

scenarios.hook: Build a Career Day for the whole class.
scenarios.relearn: A Career Day has every job, open to every kid.

scenarios.hook: Match the job to its tool.
scenarios.relearn: Every tool is for anyone who learns the job.

scenarios.hook: Be a firefighter, hero!
scenarios.relearn: Anyone brave and strong can be a firefighter, girls too.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: what do YOU want to be?
scenarios.prompt: Point to a dream (or say your own!).
scenarios.affirm: What a great dream. You can absolutely be that.
scenarios.relearn: Your dream job is yours, and it's possible.

scenarios.hook: Blast off as an astronaut!
scenarios.relearn: Anyone can reach for the stars.

scenarios.hook: Stand tall in your dress-up costume.

yourLine.text: "I can be anything I want to be!"

scenarios.relearn: Saying "I can be anything" out loud makes it feel real.

scenarios.hook: Everyone in uniform! Match the kid to the job, any kid, any job.
scenarios.relearn: Uniforms fit any kid; jobs have no gender.

scenarios.hook: Be a scientist, discover something!
scenarios.relearn: Anyone curious can be a scientist.

scenarios.hook: "Some jobs are just for boys, some just for girls."

myth.un: Some jobs are only for boys or only for girls.
myth.re: Any job is for anyone who wants to learn it.
myth.why: A job cares about skill, not gender.

scenarios.relearn: No job belongs to one gender.

scenarios.hook: "Girls can't be pilots."

myth.un: Girls can't be pilots.
myth.re: Women fly planes all over the world.
myth.why: Flying takes training, which anyone can do.

scenarios.relearn: Girls can absolutely be pilots.

scenarios.hook: "Girls can't be engineers."

myth.un: Girls can't be engineers.
myth.re: Girls design, build and invent brilliantly.
myth.why: Engineering is for any curious builder.

scenarios.relearn: Girls make wonderful engineers.

scenarios.hook: A girl says she wants to be a scientist.
scenarios.relearn: Cheering a girl's STEM dream helps her believe it.

scenarios.hook: A girl says she'll be an engineer, and a kid laughs.

options.text: Say "girls are great engineers, go for it!"
options.consequence: She stands tall and keeps her dream.

options.text: Laugh too
options.consequence: She shrinks back from a dream she'd love.

scenarios.debrief: A quick cheer can save a big dream.
scenarios.relearn: Back a girl's big dream; don't laugh it away.

scenarios.hook: "Coding isn't for girls."

myth.un: Coding isn't for girls.
myth.re: Girls code and build technology brilliantly.
myth.why: Computers don't know who's typing.

scenarios.relearn: Girls can be amazing coders.

scenarios.hook: Match each girl to the big job she dreams of.
scenarios.relearn: Girls can dream of, and reach, any of these.

scenarios.hook: "Maths is too hard for girls."

myth.un: Maths is too hard for girls.
myth.re: Girls are great at maths; practice makes anyone great.
myth.why: Ability grows with practice, not gender.

scenarios.relearn: Girls can be brilliant at maths.

scenarios.hook: A girl is unsure she can be the leader.
scenarios.relearn: Girls can lead; a cheer helps them step up.

scenarios.hook: The class is picking a leader and only naming boys.

options.text: Say "a girl could lead us too"
options.consequence: A great leader gets her chance.

options.text: Stay quiet
options.consequence: A good leader is overlooked for no reason.

scenarios.debrief: Leaders are chosen for skill, not gender.
scenarios.relearn: Girls belong in every leader role.

scenarios.hook: "Girls grow up just to cook and clean."

myth.un: Girls grow up just to cook and clean.
myth.re: Girls can grow up to be anything they choose.
myth.why: That's an old idea, not a rule.

scenarios.relearn: A girl's future is wide open.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: girls, what BIG thing do you dream of?
scenarios.prompt: Point to one (or say your own).
scenarios.affirm: That's a wonderful, reachable dream. Go for it.
scenarios.relearn: No big dream is too big for a girl.

scenarios.hook: "Girls can't do tough jobs like building or defence."

myth.un: Girls can't do tough jobs.
myth.re: Women build, serve and lead in every tough job.
myth.why: Toughness is trained, not gendered.

scenarios.relearn: Girls can do the toughest jobs there are.

scenarios.hook: "Boys can't be nurses."

myth.un: Boys can't be nurses.
myth.re: Men are wonderful nurses; caring is for everyone.
myth.why: Nursing needs care and skill, which anyone has.

scenarios.relearn: Boys can be brilliant, caring nurses.

scenarios.hook: "Boys can't be dancers."

myth.un: Boys can't be dancers.
myth.re: Boys are wonderful dancers; it takes great strength.
myth.why: Dance is power and grace, for any body.

scenarios.relearn: Boys can dance beautifully.

scenarios.hook: A boy says he wants to be a chef.
scenarios.relearn: Backing a boy's caring/arts dream helps him keep it.

scenarios.hook: A boy wants to be a nurse, and a kid teases him.

options.text: Say "nursing is a great job for anyone"
options.consequence: He stands tall and keeps his dream.

options.text: Join the teasing
options.consequence: He hides a caring dream he'd be great at.

scenarios.debrief: Caring is a strength; back the boy who wants to nurse.
scenarios.relearn: Boys who want caring jobs deserve cheering.

scenarios.hook: "Boys can't take care of babies."

myth.un: Boys can't take care of babies.
myth.re: Boys and men are great carers and dads.
myth.why: Caring is learned by anyone who tries.

scenarios.relearn: Boys can be gentle, capable carers.

scenarios.hook: Match each boy to the caring/arts job he loves.
scenarios.relearn: Boys belong in caring and arts jobs too.

scenarios.hook: "Caring jobs aren't real jobs for men."

myth.un: Caring jobs aren't real jobs for men.
myth.re: Caring jobs are real, important and great for men.
myth.why: The world needs carers; it's vital work.

scenarios.relearn: Caring work is a proud, real job for anyone.

scenarios.hook: A boy is gentle with a younger child.

yourLine.text: "You're so kind and caring, that's a strength."

scenarios.relearn: Boys can be gentle and caring; that's strength, not weakness.

scenarios.hook: A boy wants to play teacher with the little kids; others say that's for girls.

options.text: Say "anyone can be a teacher" and join in
options.consequence: He has fun and learns he can care and teach.

options.text: Tell him to stop
options.consequence: He gives up something he's good at.

scenarios.debrief: Teaching and caring are for everyone.
scenarios.relearn: Boys can teach and care wonderfully.

scenarios.hook: "A dad who stays home to care is doing it wrong."

myth.un: A stay-at-home dad is wrong.
myth.re: A dad who cares for his kids at home is wonderful.
myth.why: Caring for family is valuable, whoever does it.

scenarios.relearn: Caring dads at home are great dads.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: is it okay for a boy to dream of a caring job?
scenarios.affirm: Yes! Caring jobs are wonderful for boys and everyone.
scenarios.relearn: Caring dreams are great for boys too.

scenarios.hook: Match the caring job to why it's great.
scenarios.relearn: Caring jobs make the world kinder, great for any boy.

scenarios.hook: Home jobs: who can do them? Sort it.
scenarios.relearn: Cooking and fixing are for everyone in the family.

scenarios.hook: "Kitchen and cleaning are girls' work."

myth.un: Kitchen and cleaning are girls' work.
myth.re: Everyone helps the family; chores have no gender.
myth.why: A home runs when everyone pitches in.

scenarios.relearn: Everyone helps with home jobs.

scenarios.hook: Your brother plays while your sister does all the chores.

options.text: Say "let's all take turns"
options.consequence: Everyone helps; it's fair and faster.

options.text: Let it stay unfair
options.consequence: One kid does it all; that's not fair.

scenarios.debrief: Chores by turns, not by gender, is fair.
scenarios.relearn: Everyone in the family takes a turn.

scenarios.hook: "Boys shouldn't have to help at home."

myth.un: Boys shouldn't have to help at home.
myth.re: Boys help at home just like everyone.
myth.why: Helping is part of being in a family.

scenarios.relearn: Boys do chores too; everyone helps.

scenarios.hook: You want to pitch in at home.

yourLine.text: "I can help cook and clean too!"

scenarios.relearn: Offering to help is something anyone can do.

scenarios.hook: Sort: fair sharing of chores, or not?
scenarios.relearn: Fair homes share the work across everyone.

scenarios.hook: Match the chore to who can do it. (Trick: anyone!)
scenarios.relearn: Every chore can be done by anyone in the family.

scenarios.hook: Dadi says "let your brother rest, you help with the cooking."

options.text: Gently say "can we both take turns?"
options.consequence: Everyone helps; even dadi can smile at fair.

options.text: Do it all alone, every time
options.consequence: It's tiring and unfair over time.

scenarios.debrief: Framing it as "everyone helps the family" makes fairness easy to accept.
scenarios.relearn: It's okay to ask, kindly, for chores to be shared.

scenarios.hook: Build a fair chore chart for the family.
scenarios.prompt: Give everyone a turn at each job.
scenarios.relearn: A fair chart gives everyone a turn at every job.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: what home job could YOU help with?
scenarios.affirm: That's a great way to help your family. Everyone pitches in.
scenarios.relearn: You can be a helper at home, whoever you are.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: what's your BIG dream?
scenarios.prompt: Point to one (or say your own).
scenarios.affirm: What a wonderful dream. Let's believe in it together.
scenarios.relearn: Your big dream matters and is worth chasing.

scenarios.hook: "You can't be the first in your family to do that."

myth.un: You can't be the first in your family to do a big job.
myth.re: You can be the first; someone always is.
myth.why: Every family's first did something new.

scenarios.relearn: You can be the first in your family to follow a dream.

scenarios.hook: You dream of a job no one in your family has done. Someone says "people like us don't do that."

options.text: Keep dreaming and ask a trusted grown-up for help
options.consequence: You find a path and people who believe in you.

options.text: Give the dream up
options.consequence: A dream you'd love is lost for no good reason.

scenarios.debrief: "People like us" isn't a rule. You can be the first.
scenarios.relearn: Big dreams are for every kid, from every home.

scenarios.hook: "You're either born good at it or you're not."

myth.un: You're born good at something or you never will be.
myth.re: Skills grow with practice; anyone can get good.
myth.why: Brains and bodies learn with effort.

scenarios.relearn: Practice, not luck, builds skill.

scenarios.hook: Something is hard and you want to give up.

yourLine.text: "I can't do it YET, I'll keep practising."

scenarios.relearn: Adding "yet" turns can't into not-yet.

scenarios.hook: You tried once, it didn't work, and you want to quit.

options.text: Try again a different way
options.consequence: You get a bit better; that's how learning works.

options.text: Quit for good
options.consequence: You miss the fun part, getting good at it.

scenarios.debrief: Failing the first time is the start of learning, not the end.
scenarios.relearn: Trying again is how everyone learns.

scenarios.hook: "Failing means you're bad at it."

myth.un: Failing means you're bad at it.
myth.re: Failing is part of learning; it means you're trying.
myth.why: Every expert failed lots while learning.

scenarios.relearn: Mistakes are how we get better.

scenarios.hook: Think of something you got better at by practising.
scenarios.affirm: See, you grew that skill by practising. You can do that with anything.
scenarios.relearn: You've grown skills before; you can do it again.

scenarios.hook: "Big dreams are only for rich kids."

myth.un: Big dreams are only for rich kids.
myth.re: Every kid can dream big and work toward it.
myth.why: Dreams start with effort and help, not money alone.

scenarios.relearn: Your dream is valid, whatever home you come from.

scenarios.hook: A friend shares a big dream.

yourLine.text: "That's a great dream, you can do it!"

scenarios.relearn: Cheering a friend's dream helps it grow.

scenarios.hook: Match the dream to a first small step.
scenarios.relearn: Every big dream starts with a small first step.

scenarios.hook: Someone says your dream is silly.

options.text: Keep it and find people who believe in you
options.consequence: Your dream stays alive, with cheerleaders.

options.text: Drop it to avoid being teased
options.consequence: You lose something precious for one unkind voice.

scenarios.debrief: One unkind voice doesn't get to end your dream.
scenarios.relearn: Hold your dream; surround it with believers.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: who believes in your dream?
scenarios.affirm: Keep those believers close, and add Lensy to the list.
scenarios.relearn: Believers help dreams come true; gather yours.

scenarios.hook: "You have to know right now what you'll be."

myth.un: You must decide now what you'll be forever.
myth.re: You can dream many things and change your mind.
myth.why: Exploring lots of dreams is part of growing up.

scenarios.relearn: It's fine to dream many jobs and change later.

scenarios.hook: "Your gender decides your job."

myth.un: Your gender decides what job you can do.
myth.re: No dream is off-limits because of your gender.
myth.why: Skill and interest pick your job, not gender.

scenarios.relearn: Your gender never closes a door on a dream.

scenarios.hook: Real role models! Match each to their job.
scenarios.relearn: Real role models show anyone can do any job.

scenarios.hook: "Girls grow up to cook, boys grow up to earn."

myth.un: Girls grow up to cook; boys grow up to earn.
myth.re: Anyone can earn, care, or do both.
myth.why: That's an old idea, not a rule of life.

scenarios.relearn: Earning and caring are for everyone.

scenarios.hook: A girl says she'll be a scientist AND a mum. Someone says "you can't do both."

options.text: Say "you can have a career and a family"
options.consequence: She keeps both dreams, which is allowed.

options.text: Agree she must pick one
options.consequence: She gives up half a dream for no reason.

scenarios.debrief: A career and a family are both possible.
scenarios.relearn: You can dream of work and family together.

scenarios.hook: "Women can't be bosses or leaders."

myth.un: Women can't be bosses or leaders.
myth.re: Women lead teams, companies and countries.
myth.why: Leadership is a skill anyone can grow.

scenarios.relearn: Women make brilliant leaders.

scenarios.hook: Stand tall for your future.
scenarios.relearn: Saying "no limits" out loud builds belief.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: name a job you'd love that some people say isn't 'for you'.
scenarios.affirm: That job is absolutely for you. Old rules don't decide your future.
scenarios.relearn: You decide your future, not an old rule.

scenarios.hook: Meeting a real role model opens a dream. Match them.
scenarios.relearn: Seeing someone like you in a job makes it feel possible.

scenarios.hook: "Men can't show feelings at work."

myth.un: Men can't show feelings or be kind at work.
myth.re: Kind, caring leaders and workers are the best kind.
myth.why: Feelings make people better teammates.

scenarios.relearn: Being caring is a strength in any job.

scenarios.hook: At Career Day, kids are told to pick "gender-appropriate" jobs.

options.text: Pick the job you truly love
options.consequence: You explore a real dream, no matter the label.

options.text: Pick what you're 'supposed' to
options.consequence: You ignore what you love for an old rule.

scenarios.debrief: Pick the job you love, not the one a label assigns.
scenarios.relearn: Love, not gender, should pick your dream.

scenarios.hook: "Some people are just better because of their gender."

myth.un: One gender is just better at important jobs.
myth.re: Everyone is equal; talent grows with practice for all.
myth.why: No gender is born better at a job.

scenarios.relearn: All genders are equally capable.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: what will you say to someone who claims a job's "not for you"?
scenarios.affirm: That's a great comeback. Keep it ready.
scenarios.relearn: You can answer "not for you" with confidence.

scenarios.hook: Cheer the whole class of dreamers.
scenarios.relearn: "Anyone can be anything" is the whole game in five words.

scenarios.hook: Match each kid to their future. (Trick: any kid, any future!)
scenarios.relearn: Any kid can grow into any future.

scenarios.hook: Build YOUR dream-job outfit.
scenarios.prompt: Pick the bits for the job you love.
scenarios.relearn: Whatever job you build, it's yours to dream.

scenarios.hook: "Only boys are good with computers."

myth.un: Only boys are good with computers.
myth.re: Anyone can code, build and fix technology.
myth.why: Tech skills are learned, not gendered.

scenarios.relearn: Girls and boys are both great with tech.

scenarios.hook: A friend doubts they can reach their dream.

yourLine.text: "You can do it, I believe in you."

scenarios.relearn: Believing in a friend helps them believe in themselves.

scenarios.hook: "Helping at home is only for some kids."

myth.un: Only some kids should help at home.
myth.re: Everyone in the family helps, by turns.
myth.why: Sharing the work is fair and kind.

scenarios.relearn: Every kid can be a home helper.

scenarios.hook: Capstone: a game needs a 'captain'. The group says only a boy can.

options.text: Say "let's pick the best leader, any kid"
options.consequence: A great captain is chosen fairly; the game's better.

options.text: Let it be boys-only
options.consequence: A great leader is benched for no reason.

scenarios.debrief: Pick people for what they can do, not their gender.
scenarios.relearn: Any kid can captain; choose on skill.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: what's your Can-Do motto?
scenarios.affirm: Carry that everywhere. You really can be anything.
scenarios.relearn: Anyone can be anything, whatever their gender.
